item.title: High Surf Warning in effect through Tuesday
item.description: The National Weather Service has issued a High Surf Warning for north- and east-facing shores of Kauai and Niihau currently in effect through 6 p.m. Tuesday, Feb. 24. The warning may be extended, dropped, or modified as conditions develop.

item.title: EDITORIAL: Develop path for foreign teachers
item.description: It’s clear that the state Department of Education (DOE) is getting more reliant on visiting international educators to combat Hawaii’s chronic teacher shortage. That’s reasonable, especially since these are educators qualified to teach students in their home country, with several layers of vetting done before they are hired here.

item.title: TAX MAN: Use that hoarded tuition and fees now
item.description: We have been writing several pieces about money languishing in special funds. This week we will concentrate on one of them. The University of Hawaii has a special fund for tuition and fees. According to Department Communication 100 submitted to this year’s Legislature, that fund built up, as of June 30, 2025, almost $429 million.

item.title: Celebrating the Lunar New Year in Poipu
item.description: POIPU — Hundreds of people of all ages literally ran from all points of The Shops at Kukuiula on Friday when the first of eight big strings of firecrackers broke the calm of the afternoon.

item.title: Lei Hulu Kauai’s first graduation
item.description: LIHUE — More than 100 lei hulu, or feather lei, graced the Kauai War Memorial Convention Hall on Feb. 15 when Kumu Hulu Robin Kaheaokalani Goss and Lei Hulu Kauai graduated six haumana, or students, from around the island.

item.title: OHA to study feasibility of Native Hawaiian cultural center
item.description: The Office of Hawaiian Affairs announced today that it selected AEA Consulting to conduct a feasibility study for a proposed Native Hawaiian Cultural Center in Kaka‘ako Makai, launching what officials describe as a community-driven planning process for the long-discussed project.

item.title: Flash flooding forces evacuations with more wet weather ahead
State lawmakers try to tackle Hawaii’s teacher shortage
item.description: A measure that would create a new five-year state permit for visiting international teachers has drawn strong support from the state Department of Education as well as immigrant and educator advocates, as Hawaii continues to grapple with a persistent teacher shortage.
